chunks: And whatever is in it from Hammad Al-Nawwa', I have narrated it from Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Majilawayh - may Allah be pleased with him - from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi Al-Qasim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Khalid Al-Barqi, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Hammad Al-Nawwa'.

key_terms.ابْنُ مِسْكَانَ: Ibn Muskan, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.الْبَرْقِيُّ: Al-Barqi, referring to Muhammad ibn Khalid Al-Barqi, a famous hadith scholar
key_terms.حَمَّادٌ النَّاوِيءُ: Hammad Al-Nawwa', a prominent narrator of hadith
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him, a phrase of respect for the narrator
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ مَاجِيلَوَيْهُ: Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Majilawayh, a key narrator and compiler

ai.seo_question: Who is the narrator chain for Hammad Al-Nawwa' in Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih?
ai.summary: This passage from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih* provides a detailed *isnad* (chain of transmission) tracing the narration of Hammad al-Nawwa' back to the compiler, Shaykh al-Saduq, through a lineage of prominent Kufi and Tabi'un scholars. By explicitly linking Hammad to Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh and his ancestors, al-Saduq reinforces the reliability of this specific narrator within the Shia scholarly tradition, addressing potential concerns about the continuity and authenticity of the report.
